note: Muse's own meaning for each heuristic label. status: draft until the author locks it. detects: found (vault-wide), pile (only when your own facts show it), half (Muse finds only the start of it), none.

rows.name: Chain with pivot
rows.definition: Two or more facts handed on through a shared entity or word (the pivot): the second fact starts from what the first one ends on. One fact that merely states a cause is a link, not a chain.

rows.name: Ripple
rows.definition: One event with several downstream effects in unrelated spheres.

rows.name: Same-moment coincidence
rows.definition: Two facts from unrelated fields that fall on the same calendar day. The date is the join; the question hides the date or the other event.

rows.name: Parallel instances
rows.definition: The same role played in different places or times.

rows.name: Clone-of
rows.definition: A local or later version of a foreign original: a rebadge, a remake, a copy under another name. The link is the lineage of the thing.

rows.name: Echo / lineage / homage chain
rows.definition: Inspiration passed on across works, media or cultures in two or three hops, including through an intermediary such as a translation. Each hop is a stated imitation or descent.

rows.name: Namesake split
rows.definition: One person's name appearing in two unlike entities; a stage name or brand derived from a predecessor.

rows.name: Name borrowed across places or eras
rows.definition: A name carried from one place or time to another, usually by people who moved, and now meaning something new in the new place.

rows.name: Why-here / chosen-because
rows.definition: The reason a place, person or moment was picked: a political, practical or accidental condition, not geography alone.

rows.name: Persists-as (afterlife)
rows.definition: How something survives in a changed form.

rows.name: Legend explains practice (aetiology)
rows.definition: A legend or story that accounts for a custom, rule or object that still exists. The answer is the story or the practice it explains.

rows.name: Old text, new headline
rows.definition: A historical record that echoes a current news story.

rows.name: Knowledge import
rows.definition: A solution studied in one place or field and applied in another. The link is the import: who looked, where, and what they took.

rows.name: Constraint becomes signature
rows.definition: A practical limit, accident or ethical choice yields a famous trait.

rows.name: Neglected discovery with a reason
rows.definition: A finding ignored or unrecognised because of language, medium, politics or status, and used later. The reason it was ignored is the hook.

rows.name: Commemoration channels
rows.definition: A figure honoured through currency, mountain, park, award or logo.

rows.name: Rehabilitation
rows.definition: A figure or site long ignored, now restored.

rows.name: Trigger event
rows.definition: A small act igniting a large consequence.

rows.name: Cause cascade
rows.definition: A multi-step decline or collapse.

rows.name: Bio-cultural mechanism
rows.definition: A habit or biological property shaping politics, economy or daily rhythm.

rows.name: Mechanism reuse
rows.definition: The same physical or chemical process in unrelated contexts.

rows.name: Shape explains function
rows.definition: A geometry or engineering reason.

rows.name: Design against nature
rows.definition: A material or form chosen as a statement about nature.

rows.name: Human-uniqueness boundary
rows.definition: A behaviour once thought uniquely human, found elsewhere.

rows.name: Institutional quirk
rows.definition: A surprising rule or protocol.

rows.name: Fiction-embedded real thing
rows.definition: A real place or object made for a fiction; real people portrayed or thinly veiled.

rows.name: Myth propagated by art / claim provenance
rows.definition: A popular belief, where it first appeared, and whether the source said it.

rows.name: Contested or dual explanation
rows.definition: Both stories plus a confidence flag.

rows.name: Anomaly in a corpus
rows.definition: The outlier, the unique signature.

rows.name: Named exception in a free form
rows.definition: A fixed element inside a fluid structure.

rows.name: Behind-the-scenes decision
rows.definition: Props, costumes, effects and production choices.

rows.name: Counterfactual pivot
rows.definition: One event that could have gone otherwise.

rows.name: Perspective shift
rows.definition: The story from the other party or a minor character.

rows.name: Decision with ethics
rows.definition: Declining a patent, opening a design, refusing a perk.

rows.name: Small physical detail carrying weight
rows.definition: The heart-bearing memorial detail.

rows.name: Uniqueness claims
rows.definition: A first, only, largest or otherwise extreme within a stated class. The claim only holds with its class, so the class must be named.

rows.name: Series pattern
rows.definition: Streak, dominance, gap or count in a table or list.

rows.name: Material x occasion
rows.definition: A material tied to a particular occasion or event: what something was made of, and what it was made for.

rows.name: Lesser-known achievement
rows.definition: A creditable achievement of a well-known person that few people know about.

rows.name: Hidden kinship, shared school, shared epithet
rows.definition: Two people or things linked by a hidden kinship, a shared school or a shared epithet, so the link surprises.

rows.name: Internal duality
rows.definition: One entity with two contrasting properties.

rows.name: Analogy bridge
rows.definition: Explaining a convention through an unrelated domain's convention.

rows.name: The incidental aside
rows.definition: The best seed is often a digression in a text, not its main claim.

rows.name: Visual resemblance joke
rows.definition: A building, logo or object that looks like something unexpected.

rows.name: Etymology unveil
rows.definition: A word whose plain-language root or origin is the point: the answer is the word, the clue is where it comes from (a loanword, a root, a brand made from a phrase).

rows.name: Name as description
rows.definition: An animal, organ, instrument or tool named for a trait, size or shape in some language.

rows.name: Number, colour or material inside a name
rows.definition: A number, a colour or a material hidden inside a name.

rows.name: Polysemy / homonym collision
rows.definition: One word or name with several unrelated worlds. The question turns on a sense the solver did not expect.

rows.name: Near-homophone or one-letter-off pair
rows.definition: Two names that sound alike or differ by one letter, so one reads as a parody or a pun on the other.

rows.name: Shared morpheme across paired names
rows.definition: A word part shared by two names that look unrelated, such as the same ending in two river names.

rows.name: Backronym, initials-as-name, pun-title, idiom-pun, rhyme-derived title
rows.definition: A title or name built from initials, a pun, an idiom or a rhyme; the expansion or the wordplay is the point.

rows.name: Eponym and its reversal or change
rows.definition: A name taken from a person, where the namesake is not the original or the use has since been reversed or changed.

rows.name: Term migration
rows.definition: A word changing domain over centuries.

rows.name: Name from a habit or deed
rows.definition: A name that comes from what its bearer did or habitually does.

rows.name: "Not named for X"
rows.definition: The false friend, the folk misattribution.

rows.name: Logo or brand hiding a story
rows.definition: A logo or brand mark with a backstory most people do not know.

rows.name: Renaming
rows.definition: After independence, a change of official language, a rebrand stunt (adding or dropping letters).

rows.name: Cryptic composition
rows.definition: Answers whose letters concatenate, interleave or hide a third word; anagrams; hidden words.

rows.name: Shared phrase across logos or entities
rows.definition: The same phrase used by unrelated entities, such as logos, companies or events.

rows.name: Digit, date or homophone wordplay
rows.definition: Digits, dates or homophones recomposed into a title or name.

rows.name: Connect
rows.definition: Many clues, one hidden link; the link is often a lateral set, a former role, or a polyseme.

rows.name: Reveal-last theme
rows.definition: Several independently answerable items, and a final item names the hidden theme.

rows.name: Superlative-list pair
rows.definition: "what is it" plus "what list does it top".

rows.name: Dual-path hint
rows.definition: A description plus a cross-domain nudge that triangulates the same answer.

rows.name: Ladder of obscurity
rows.definition: Clues ordered hard to easy.

rows.name: Split answers
rows.definition: Two or three sub-answers, sometimes order-sensitive.

rows.name: Set-level spine
rows.definition: A whole set organised by a region, theme or occasion (a lens at set scale).

rows.name: Breadth sweep versus deep multi-hop
rows.definition: High-volume single-hop items, deep chains for written rounds, tiers for audience and spares.

rows.name: Cryptic round format
rows.definition: A round whose answers are built by a cryptic rule (see Cryptic composition) instead of by a topic.

rows.name: Scratchpad state
rows.definition: Several raw related facts plus "is there a question in this?" This is the target spark-card shape.

rows.name: Media-dependent items
rows.definition: (image, audio, video recognition): out of scope for a text vault; the Muse can only note them.
